name: QUEST Integration Self-Direction (Consumer-Directed Personal Assistance)
summary: Hawaii's Medicaid program, QUEST Integration, covers long-term services at home through health plans. Members who need nursing-facility-level care can choose self-direction for personal assistance and attendant care, which lets them hire, train and supervise their own worker, including a family member. The health plan pays the worker, and a fiscal agent handles payroll taxes.
who_qualifies: Hawaii resident enrolled in Med-QUEST (Hawaii Medicaid) through a QUEST Integration health plan; no age limit.
Needs nursing facility level of care for full home and community-based services; people found only 'at risk' get a smaller set of services.
Meets Medicaid financial rules — reported as $1,530/month income and $2,000 in assets for an individual in 2026.
Lives at home, not in a nursing facility.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — Med-QUEST's self-direction protocol says family members may be hired.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: yes — a Med-QUEST protocol says HCBS participants can hire family members including spouses; this dates from the earlier QExA program, so confirm with your health plan.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: limited — the same Med-QUEST protocol lists parents of minors as allowed hires under QExA, but current QUEST Integration rules on paying parents are not clearly published; confirm with Med-QUEST.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the worker does not have to live with the member.

pay.detail: Med-QUEST does not publish a self-directed wage. Third-party reports put pay at about $14–$23/hour depending on plan and island, up to about $3,028/month. The state let health plans pay self-directed workers once a month (within 10 days after the pay period ends) under a labor department exception.

hours_or_budget: The health plan's service coordinator assesses the member and authorizes personal assistance or attendant care hours in the service plan.

waitlist.detail: Medicaid enrollment is an entitlement, but home and community-based service slots can be limited, so a wait for HCBS can occur when slots are full.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Members can use agency providers or self-direct. In self-direction the member, guardian or representative is the managing employer; the health plan pays the worker and a financial management services agency handles taxes. Members who self-direct also name backup agency providers.
how_to_apply: Apply for Med-QUEST online at medical.mybenefits.hawaii.gov, by phone at 1-800-316-8005, or with form DHS 1100 mailed or faxed to a Med-QUEST eligibility office.
Choose or get assigned a QUEST Integration health plan.
Ask the health plan for a long-term services and supports assessment (level of care).
Tell the service coordinator you want to self-direct personal assistance and name the person you want to hire; complete the hiring paperwork and background checks.

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for a family member in Hawaii?
faqs.a: Yes. If the person is on QUEST Integration and qualifies for home and community-based services, they can self-direct and hire a family member as their personal assistance worker.
A Med-QUEST protocol says family members, including spouses, may be hired. That protocol is from the earlier QExA program, so ask your health plan to confirm before you start.

faqs.q: How much do self-directed workers earn in Hawaii?
faqs.a: Med-QUEST does not publish a rate. Reports put pay around $14 to $23 an hour, depending on the plan and island.

faqs.q: How often are self-directed workers paid?
faqs.a: Health plans may pay once a month under a state labor department exception, but they must pay within 10 days after each pay period ends.

faqs.q: Who do I ask about self-direction?
faqs.a: Your QUEST Integration health plan's service coordinator. If you are not on Med-QUEST yet, apply first by calling 1-800-316-8005.
